voice.persona: an experienced My Clinic colleague coaching a learner in their first week

segments.narration: OMAR: Welcome to Who Does What: Operations & My Care. You will practise decisions that help you act with confidence. You will leave with practical actions for your next shift.

OMAR: Routing matters. A patient who repeats their story loses trust. I once sent the same patient to three desks in one morning. She never forgot it — and neither did I. Keep the main point connected to a familiar task or conversation. That connection makes the information easier to use when it matters. Use the principle in context.
segments.on_screen_text: "Right team, first time." · A patient shouldn't have to tell their story twice.

segments.narration: OMAR: Walk the journey. Notice where each team leads. Let each marker add context rather than rushing to a conclusion. The full picture matters before a workplace decision is made. Keep the next action clear. Think of the first detail you would check. Apply the point to a familiar task.
segments.on_screen_text: Horizontal journey: Book → Arrive & register → Consult → Lab / Radiology / Pharmacy → Leave → Follow-up. Each stage shows which team leads (Operations, My Care or both)

segments.narration: OMAR: Operations runs the day: environment, KPIs, recovery on the spot. Use each section to build the picture step by step. Before moving on, identify the action or check that belongs to your role. Apply the point to a familiar task. Carry the idea into your next decision. Pause and connect this to your role. Use the principle in context. Keep the next action clear. Think of the first detail you would check. Apply the point to a familiar task. Carry the idea into your next decision. Pause and connect this to your role.
